hook.line: Saturday at the café is a different animal: Tomás cannot find a free table, and he has to say so to Vale in half a second.
hook.es: El café está lleno a reventar.
hook.en: The café is packed to bursting.

rule:
To say something is completely full, use *lleno a reventar*: full until it bursts.

It works for places, containers and crowds: *El café estaba lleno a reventar.*

Two more ways to say it:
*lleno hasta el tope* (full to the top): *El bus iba lleno hasta el tope.*
*repleto de* (crammed with): *La nevera está repleta de comida.*

*Lleno* agrees with what it describes: *llena a reventar* for *la maleta*. *A reventar* itself never changes.

English says "packed" or "jam-packed". The Spanish picture is bursting.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an intensifying phrase (*locución intensificadora*). *Reventar* means to burst.

options: The stadium was empty.
The stadium was packed to bursting.
The stadium burst into flames.

options: The bus went to the top of the hill.
The bus was nearly empty.
The bus was packed.

options: The fridge is crammed with food.

The fridge is on top of the food.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *lleno* or *llena*: La maleta está ___ a reventar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: La maleta está llena a reventar.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *lleno* or *llena*: El estadio estaba ___ a reventar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: El estadio estaba lleno a reventar.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "The café was packed to bursting on Saturday."
yourTurn.answer: El café estaba lleno a reventar el sábado.
yourTurn.why: *Estaba lleno a reventar* describes the crowd at that moment in the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "The bus was packed." Use *hasta el tope*.
yourTurn.answer: El bus iba lleno hasta el tope.
accept: El bus iba hasta el tope.
yourTurn.why: *Hasta el tope* is the "to the top" way to say it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "My phone is crammed with photos."
yourTurn.answer: Mi celular está repleto de fotos.
yourTurn.why: *Repleto de* is followed by what fills it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "The fridge is crammed with food."
yourTurn.answer: La nevera está repleta de comida.
yourTurn.why: *Repleta* agrees with *nevera*, and *de* introduces the content.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *La calle estaba llena a reventar.* Say "The streets were packed to bursting."
yourTurn.answer: Las calles estaban llenas a reventar.
yourTurn.why: *Lleno* agrees in number and gender, but *a reventar* does not change.

pitfalls.wrong: El café estaba lleno por reventar.
pitfalls.right: El café estaba lleno a reventar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase uses *a*, not *por*.

pitfalls.wrong: La maleta está lleno a reventar.
pitfalls.right: La maleta está llena a reventar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Lleno* must agree with *maleta*, so it is *llena*.

pitfalls.wrong: La nevera está repleta con comida.
pitfalls.right: La nevera está repleta de comida.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "crammed with", but *repleto* takes *de*.
